evidence: Supplied GET_TSK_INFO API forms and authored offline task/scheduler tests; no native task inspection

sources.topic: GET_TSK_INFO directional identity operands, INTEGER/STRING value outputs, 21 TSK attributes, PG status and program-type names

implemented.lookup: Case-insensitive registered name when number is zero/uninitialized; otherwise one-based registry order shared with numeric controls
implemented.outputs: Only selected identity and selected INTEGER/STRING output change on success; failures write status only; exact disjoint writable references
implemented.live: Caller-rooted source module/routine frames, latest checkpoint line, logical frame count, task/program state and scheduler quantum
implemented.metadata: Fourteen remaining documented INTEGER attributes can be supplied explicitly during binding; live attributes cannot be overridden
implemented.ownership: Input/reference capture order, source guards, independent concurrent linked stacks, cleanup on completion/failure/stop and value-free operation records

portable_choices: Package TSK IDs 1..21, PG task-state IDs 100..108 and program-type IDs 200..202 do not assert native encodings
Additional PG_COMPLETED/PG_STOPPED/PG_FAILED/PG_WAITING names preserve existing runtime state distinctions
TSK_STACK counts logical active routine frames, including external declaration proxies, rather than native allocation bytes
TSK_LINENUM is the most recent source checkpoint and is zero before execution; it is not a native instruction pointer
Unmodeled attributes require explicit informational metadata; they do not change task scheduling/control
Portable status 0 success, 1 unknown task, 2 invalid selector, 3 missing metadata; failed inspection preserves data/identity outputs
No implicit task discovery or binding; host task configuration/continuations are omitted from value snapshots
remaining: Native enum/task-number/stack layout, parent-child discovery, priority and interrupt execution, motion state, strict mode and native acceptance
